artefact: MAINLINE demo-api deployment package - served-tree shape, before and after
caveats: The whole-package before/after deltas are NOT purely this change, and the `after` sha256 has a shelf life. mainline_demo_api/ went 11 entries / 283,402 B (before) -> 11 / 320,353 B -> 12 / 333,886 B during the hours this was measured, because other workers in this same wave own that package. Take the zip hash from the build you run, not from this file. The web/ figures ARE clean: dist/ and the sealed evidence bundle did not move, the builder's own census reports 75 entries / 3,571,990 B before any strip -- exactly what the pre-change zips carried -- and web_tree_sha256 is identical in all eight builds across both rounds.

289,312 B of siblings is package weight paid once per deployment against 2,586,960 B of egress removed per served map. The trade is only favourable because the package is uploaded rarely and served often; it is stated here rather than assumed.
The .gz siblings bound BYTES, not RATE. A caller can still pull the 124,127 B compressed asset as fast as Lambda will answer. The rate bound is W4's and the stop is W5's; neither is in this file.

A pre-compressed sibling is only cheaper if the handler serves it. Until W3's content negotiation lands, these 57 objects are 289,312 B of package that nothing reads, and the honest reading of this file is 'the strip has landed, the compression has not yet'.

compressible_types.why: The gzipped list is exactly the entries static_site.MEDIA_TYPES marks as text, JavaScript, JSON, SVG or wasm. The left_alone list is the rest of that table: already-compressed containers, where a second pass costs package bytes and build time and saves nothing on the wire. The served tree today happens to contain none of the second list, so the exclusion was falsified against a synthetic tree carrying one file of every type - see checks.

determinism.claim: Consecutive builds of a fixed tree, by either builder, produce the same bytes; and the served tree this worker owns is reproducible independently of the rest of the package.
determinism.gzip_header_is_the_reason_this_holds: 1f 8b 08 00 00 00 00 00 02 ff on every one of the 57 siblings, in every package built. gzip.compress() was NOT used: it takes the OS byte from the zlib the interpreter was linked against, so the same input would hash differently on the Windows workstation and a Linux runner and source_code_hash would move for a reason that is not content.
determinism.how: build_lambda.sh --arch <a> into out/lambda, then into two directories outside the repository, then build_lambda.ps1 -Arch <a> into a third. All four hashed. The out-of-tree builds passed --wheelhouse at the in-tree wheelhouse so the wheels were the same known bytes rather than a second resolution from PyPI. Then the whole exercise a second time, after another worker changed mainline_demo_api/ underneath it.

served_tree_is_stable_across_both_rounds.same_in: all 8 builds, both architectures, both rounds
served_tree_is_stable_across_both_rounds.what_it_is: sha256 over the sorted (entry name, entry sha256) pairs of every web/ entry. The whole-zip hash is a statement about the whole tree and moved between the two rounds because someone else's file moved. This number did not, and it is the one that says whether the strip and the 57 siblings are reproducible.

measured_on: the project Windows workstation, CPython 3.13.14, zlib 1.3.1

packer.how_verified: The staging/pruning/packing program is embedded in build_lambda.sh (heredoc) and build_lambda.ps1 (here-string). Both normalise it to LF, write it UTF-8 without a BOM, and print its sha256. Extracted from both files by the same rules each builder applies and compared byte for byte: equal.
packer.owner_note: evidence/deploy/lambda-bundle.json still records the previous digest and the previous zip hashes. That file is not this worker's; the deltas it needs are reported to W8 rather than written here.

what_changed.not_changed: No authentication was added and no URL was gated. The console dist/ and the sealed evidence bundle were not touched: the identity bytes under web/ are the same bytes, under the same names, as before.
what_changed.one: --strip-source-maps / -StripSourceMaps became the DEFAULT, and the opt-out is --keep-source-maps / -KeepSourceMaps. The mechanism already existed; this flipped which way it points and rewrote the header comment that argued for keeping the maps. That argument was sound while the package was something an operator downloaded and is not sound for a tree served from a Function URL with authorization_type = NONE.
what_changed.two: Interface I1: every compressible web/** entry now has a <name>.gz sibling in the package. gzip level 9, MTIME 0, FLG 0 (no filename in the header), XFL 2, OS 255 (unknown, so the artefact is not a statement about the machine that built it). static_site.py owns serving them and owes a 404 on a direct request for a .gz path.
